chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn Saeed, from Yunus, from one of his men, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who said to his wife, 'You are to me like the back of my mother,' or 'like her hand,' or 'like her belly,' or 'like her private part,' or 'like herself,' or 'like her heel.' Does that constitute Zahaar, and does it necessitate upon him what necessitates the perpetrator of Zahaar? He said: The perpetrator of Zahaar, when he does Zahaar from his wife, saying 'She is like the back of his mother,' or 'her hand,' or 'her leg,' or 'her hair,' or 'anything from her,' intending by that the prohibition, then the expiation becomes obligatory upon him in every little or much of it. And similarly, when he says it to some of the close relatives (for marriage), the expiation becomes obligatory upon him.

key_terms.التَّحْرِيم: Prohibition: The legal status of being forbidden, specifically referring to the marital prohibition triggered by Zahaar.
key_terms.الظِّهَار: Zahaar: A form of divorce where a husband likens his wife's back to his mother's back, prohibiting sexual relations until expiation is made.
key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةُ: Expiation: The ritual penalty or act of atonement required after committing Zahaar.
key_terms.ذَوَاتِ الْمَحَارِم: Close female relatives with whom marriage is permanently prohibited.

ai.seo_question: What phrases constitute Zahaar and require expiation in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the legal status of Zahaar is determined by the husband's intent to prohibit intimacy, regardless of whether he compares his wife to his mother or to other close relatives (dhawāt al-maḥārim) with whom marriage is forbidden. This ruling establishes that the expiation (kaffarah) is obligatory for any specific body part mentioned, emphasizing the precision required in marital vows within Shia jurisprudence. The hadith underscores the theological link between verbal declaration and legal consequence, reinforcing the sanctity of the marital bond.
